metadata.title: Command Integrity

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for ensuring that commands received by a device are authentic, intact, attributable, and bounded prior to execution.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Command channels, control interfaces, embedded controllers, actuators, robotics, autonomous systems, and cyber‑physical command paths.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Foundational Zero Trust pattern defining integrity expectations for device commands independent of safety or authorization.

props.name: data-pattern
props.remarks: Defines command integrity signals as execution‑relevant data, not as permission, intent, or safety approval.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Establishes baseline expectations for integrity of device commands and software interactions.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Guidance for protecting device command paths and preventing unauthorized control.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Zero Trust guidance asserting that all command execution must be explicitly mediated and verified.

metadata.remarks: Command Integrity defines the baseline expectations for command authenticity, integrity, and attribution prior to execution by a device. This pattern does not determine whether a command is authorized, safe, appropriate, or permitted within a given operational context.

components.title: Command Authenticity
components.description: Ensures commands received by a device originate from a verifiable source.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Commands are cryptographically or logically bound to an identifiable source.

components.title: Command Integrity Protection
components.description: Detection of command modification or tampering between source and device execution.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Command data is protected against unauthorized modification.

components.title: Command Attribution
components.description: Ability to attribute executed commands to a specific device identity, controller, or origin.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Executed commands are attributable for audit and analysis.

components.title: Command Bounding
components.description: Constrains commands to expected syntax, structure, timing, or declared interface.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Commands are bounded to defined interfaces and execution contexts.

components.title: Command Integrity Non‑Equivalence Constraints
components.description: Explicitly defines what a valid or well‑formed command does not grant or imply.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Command integrity does not imply authorization, safety, correctness, or operational approval.
